text: having conducted numerous coding question interviews id like to offer some insights from the interviewers perspective it seems you likely struggled in the first two coding rounds also in my experience rejection notice wouldnt take three weeks unless you were strong contender two general points the biggest issue arises when an overprepared applicant the competitive coder type receives straightforward question they recognize and immediately dives in without much communication whether they go down the wrong path or not is secondary what matters most is seeing how candidate tackles an unfamiliar problem its not just about reaching the solution remember the interviewer already knows the answer theyre interested in your approach bonus if you recognize an interview question from practice etc tell the interviewer immediately solving it instantly wastes their time forcing them to ask another question with less time pretending you dont know it wont work programmers are bad actors and theyll be even more frustrated most interviewers have backup questions prepared as for the nodding and letting you make mistakes thats normal for good interviewer interviewing is like walking dog you let them explore bit reeling them in when needed but not holding them too tightly often candidates explain their intended solution and you know its wrong but you let them proceed unless theyve misunderstood the problem to see what happens interviewers find this hard because they must suppress their helpful instincts which they use daily at work nods smiles and remarks like mmh interesting or okay arent positive or negative signals theyre just polite gestures dont get overconfident realize youre on your own at that moment the same applies to general conversation the interviewer might ask probing questions but generally wont add anything new only helping you think or bounce ideas like playing tennis with wall its mostly about letting you succeed or fail independently remember the interviewer isnt trying to help theyre trying not to help corollary if the interviewer gives helpful tip youre likely behind schedule good interviewer will subtly insert the text: ive interviewed many many candidates on coding questions so this is bit of the perspective from the other side think you probably failed most on the first coding interviews also afaik it would not have taken weeks to get the rejection if you were not close to getting an offer two general comments the worst thing is when an overly prepared candidate competitive coder type is given relatively easy or familiar question and then just jumps into it without communicating much whether they take wrong turn or not doesnt really matter the most valuable thing is to get an opportunity to see how candidate works through problem they dont know already or isnt immediately obvious to them its really not about arriving at the solution the best thing to remember the destination is already known to the interviewer the journey is the interesting bit bonus tip if you get question in an interview that you already know from practice or whatever would highly recommend that you just tell the interviewer right away if you just bust out the solution quickly he will be annoyed at the waste of time because he will have to ask another question and with less time if you try to pretend you dont know the question he will see through that believe me programmers make terrible actors and he will be even more annoyed most interviewers have many alternative questions ready to go and about the nodding and letting you go astray thats typical even expected of any decent interviewer would say doing an interview is bit like walking dog you gotta let the candidate wander around bit on their own and reel them in at times but you cant just hold them on tight leash the whole time because then you dont learn anything about them very often candidates will explain what they intend to do to solve the problem and you know its wrong but you nod along and let them do it unless theyve misunderstood the problem thats just cutting them some slack to see what happens for interviewers this is really hard to do because you constantly have to repress your natural instinct to be helpful and cooperative which is what you do all the time when youre actually working things like nods smiles and timid remarks like mmh interesting or okay are not positive signals that youre on the right path or wrong path for that matter theyre just polite repressed gestures to stay friendly and passive so dont get too confident but instead understand that at that moment youre entirely on your own either shining or screwing up the same goes for general backandforth the interviewer might probe little bit with questions and stuff but you will notice that they generally dont actively add anything new just helping you think on your own or have someone to bounce ideas like playing tennis with brick wall but again its mostly about letting you make it or break it on your own so heres another thing to remember the interviewer is not trying to help you but trying his best not to help you obvious corollary if the interviewer actually gives you really helpful tip its probably because youre falling behind on time good interviewer will drop the tip during the general backandforth so you dont notice that the idea came from him but if he has to interrupt you entirely to give you an obvious tip youre probably really far off and also that youre not doing well on communication either because its probably not his first attempt at giving you that tip

architectural style used in designing networked applications particularly web services key concepts of rest api resources in the rest architecture everything is treated as resource these resources can be objects data or services that the api provides access to each resource is uniquely identified by uniform resource identifier uri http verbs rest apis use standard http methods to perform actions on resources the most common http methods used in restful apis are get retrieve data from the server post create new resource on the server put update an existing resource or create new resource if it contain all the information needed to understand and fulfill the request the server does not store any client state between requests representation resources in rest api can have multiple applications the interaction between server and client is structured similarly to how one would navigate web pages most socalled rest apis require separate documentation such as swagger or openapi which developers must consult and integrate into code that essentially generates http requests however in proper rest environment client indicates its capabilities via the accept request header and the server will respond using format compatible with the client this is known as contenttype negotiation the format is defined by media type that dictates the syntax and semantics of messagesdocuments exchanged basic json does not specify links or resource properties html for instance utilizes tags with specification defining their valid usage and permissible content server can employ html to guide client on subsequent actions for example response might include links or form sections typically with linkrelation name to contextualize the referenced resource on paginated list relations like first next prev last or self are common examples html forms provide information on the required http operation the target url and the media type often implicitly given as applicationxwformurlencoded furthermore it teaches the client about resource properties eliminating the need for external documentation with the form being dynamic new resource properties can be added the form will dynamically notify clients because they support the media type they will know how to handle new elementsproperties added to resource major issue with many selfproclaimed rest apis is that they utilize typed resources rather than sending the resource state in representation format supported by the client after contenttype negotiation these apis transmit predefined data structures which clients often implement directly without variation consequently if the response changes the client wont be able to handle the new data in the bestcase scenario the additional data will be ignored and in the worstcase scenario it will break down consequently rest architecture is typically most effective for serverside applications that serve multitude of diverse clients especially those not under your direct control since decoupling clients and servers is core rest objective adapting to change and ensuring futureproof processing is ingrained in its design for simple frontendtobackend communications text: there is an important nuance between process and thread modern computer operating systems because very old operating systems didnt do this support concept of memory protection that is to say that one process is allocated some of the main memory ram for its code instructions in some operating systems they refer to these as text pages rather than code pages they are the same idea and data things like variables not code if second process attempts to access memory that was not allocated to it that process will get segmentation violation attempt to access data outside its assigned memory segment this prevents two different processes from overwriting each others data but things are different in threads here two threads forked from the same process share the same memory the smallest chunk of memory that program can read or write is page this is architecture dependent is common size but it could be etc suppose have variable an integer its value is this only requires one byte of memory although on modern os the integer might occupy several bytes but even bit integer would only occupy bytes assume that is bytes on pagesize of bytes there are lot of other variables that occupy the same page in ram this creates problem suppose there are two completely different variables but they happen to reside within the same page two different threads could read the value of their variable but they really have to read the entire page and then disregard everything except the few bytes they care about meanwhile suppose they both modify their respective but unique variables whichever thread writes last because write back to main memory also writes the entire page wipes out everything except the few bytes that were changed this means whichever thread wrote the page last will wipe out the change of the other thread this is problem to solve this modern operating systems have concept of mutual exclusion lock on memory page the same way that multiuser database might do row locking or column locking unix operating systems handle this with something called mutual exclusion lock mtx if two threads try to access the same page for purposes of modification then when the first thread reads the page it will also apply mutual exclusion lock typically the first bit on the page is reserved for this purpose if that bit is set to then the page is locked if second thread attempts to access the page it will be told to wait until the mutex bit is cleared spin on mutex or smtx condition in multiprocessing two different processes this isnt problem because they dont share the same memory segments but in multithreading the threads do share the same memory segments so it is possible for different threads to step on each others toes and the os is designed to protect against this btw the whole point of multithreading had to do with efficiency processors are very fast if the data they have to manipulate is already in the processor registers but if the data resides elsewhere if it has to fetch the data from ram or gasp storage then the amount of clock cycles until that fetch or read completes is veritable eternity for the cpu so it may as well be put to good use doing something else multithreading vastly made programs more efficient because they could do something while longrunning steps such as memory io or storage io were being performed was completed single processor core that is capable of multithreading aka hyperthreading even within the same core cannot technically execute both threads at the same time if scheduled to execute on the same core
